correctness.rationale: The six-variable circumcircle parametrization x_j=c+r u(θ_j) has Jacobian |det|=2 area(T_θ) r³ for ordered noncollinear triples. Integrating over centers c for which all three points lie in K gives area(K⊖r T). For fixed C² boundary with curvature bounded away from zero, signed tubular normal coordinates show area(K⊖rT)=A−r∫∂K h_T(n) ds+O_K(r²), uniformly over unit-disk-contained triangles T; no requirement that the circle itself lies in K. Independent SymPy integration gives ∫sin a J(a) da=3π/8 and ∫sin²a J(a) da=8/9, yielding E[area(T)]=3/(2π), E[area(T)perimeter(T)]=64/(3π²). Rotation averaging using Cauchy’s perimeter formula gives angular integrals 24π² and 512P/3. Integrating r³ and r⁴ yields the two coefficients with O_K(t⁶). Fixed-area isoperimetric P≥2√(πA), strictly for nondisks, gives eventual strict comparison, with K-dependent cutoff. The proof is analytic; finite Jacobian spot-check or Monte Carlo not substitutes.

value.rationale: A natural random-triangle statistic encodes the first two Euclidean intrinsic volumes in its low-radius tail, giving a new local stochastic isoperimetric comparison and an exact universal boundary correction. This is a structural all-shape asymptotic, not a small-case coefficient chosen without motivation.

final_claim: For any fixed planar convex C² body of positive curvature, three uniform random points have circumradius distribution P(ρ≤t)=6π² t⁴/A(K)²−512 P(K)t⁵/(15 A(K)³)+O_K(t⁶) as t↓0, for the ordinary unconstrained circumcircle. The first two coefficients recover area and perimeter and yield pointwise eventual equal-area disk maximality.
